input.title: Where should carts live: Redis or Postgres?
input.body:
Carts currently sit in a 4 KB session cookie, so long carts get truncated. Moving the cart contents server-side and leaving only a cart ID in the cookie fixes that. The question is which store holds the carts.

**Example:** a shopper adds 40 items across several visits. Today the cookie overflows and the last items vanish. With either option, the cookie holds a short ID and the full cart is loaded from the store.

**Redis:** very fast reads and writes, and key expiry (TTL) handles abandoned carts automatically. Downsides: it is another service to run, memory is limited and may evict data, and carts are lost unless persistence is configured. Best if carts are truly disposable.

**Postgres:** carts are durable, can be queried (abandoned-cart reports, support lookups), and need no new infrastructure if you already run it. Downsides: slightly slower per request, and you need a cleanup job to delete old carts. Best if carts matter to the business.

**My pick:** Postgres, assuming you already run it. Cart traffic is modest, so the speed gap won't matter, and durable, queryable carts are worth more than the TTL convenience. Choose Redis only if you don't want carts in your database at all or you are fine losing them.

content.text:
A1 [open] decision: Where should carts live: Redis or Postgres?
actions: a1 resolve "Use Postgres (Recommended)", a2 resolve "Use Redis"
